title: "V0017 field_outside_record"
description: "A block statement is headed name: …, an anonymous record literal's field (design §17.297 (6), §17.305 (3))."
---

An error from the `parse` phase. `sakura explain V0017` prints this explanation offline.

A block statement is headed `name: …`, an anonymous record literal's field (design §17.297 (6),
§17.305 (3)). `{ request: 0, cap: 0 }` in expression position is a block, not a record: Sakura
Lang has no anonymous records, so a record literal names its type. Each `name: …` is one record
at the name, whether or not `name` is in scope, and the value up to the next `,` or the line's
end is skipped. Declare a record type and name it in the literal.

Wrong:

```sakura
let c = { request: 0, cap: 0 }
```

Fixed:

```sakura
type Budget = { request: Int, cap: Int }
let c = Budget { request: 0, cap: 0 }
```

## Wrong program

[`compiler/tests/ui/V0017_anonymous_record_literal.sak`](https://github.com/icantcodefyi/sakuralang/blob/main/compiler/tests/ui/V0017_anonymous_record_literal.sak), which the compiler's ui suite runs through `sakura check`:

```sakura
// §17.294 WP-6, §17.297 (6), §17.305 (3): `{ request: 0, cap: 0 }` in expression position is a
// block, so each `name: …` is reported once at its name and the parser takes the value up to the
// next `,` or the line's end with it: a k-field literal is k `V0017`, with no `V0009` cascade. The
// message says a record literal names its type, no `import std/llm.{request}` is offered though
// std/llm exports a `request`, and a name that resolves (`cap` below) is reported all the same.
pub fn budget() -> Int {
  let c = { request: 0, cap: 0 }
  let cap = 1
  let d = {
    request: List.len([1, 2])
    cap: cap
  }
  0
}
```
